solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Money only for material

parts.note: cash is ready money
mere means only, as in 'a mere child'

explanation.surface: Someone insists they bought the cloth purely for the money.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is a fine soft wool fabric, a kind of cloth.

clue.text: Earth, good and spherical

parts.note: something spherical is round

explanation.surface: A description of our planet: a fine place, and shaped like a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth in the sense of soil or the land underfoot is the ground.

clue.text: Story, last part recited

indicators.note: recited means spoken out, so the word for last part is heard rather than written

parts.note: the tail is the last part of something, such as a procession

explanation.surface: Someone reads out only the ending of a story.
explanation.definitionFit: A tale is a narrative, synonymous with a story.

clue.text: Energy producer held up by so many delays

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the contained letters are read from bottom to top
held says the letters are contained within the words that follow, across the word breaks

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A power station kept offline by one hold-up after another.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave 'held up' to the reversal alone, leaving the hiding unsignalled: 'held' contains the letters in 'so many delays' and 'up' turns them upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a generator that turns motion into electrical power.

clue.text: Winger on fire getting second of goals

parts.note: something on fire is flaming

indicators.note: second of picks the second letter of the word goals

explanation.surface: A football winger in brilliant form, scoring a second goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests football; here it means a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A flamingo is a wading bird, and any bird is a creature with wings.

clue.text: Brook runs into vapour

indicators.note: into says the runs letter goes inside the vapour word

parts.note: steam is water vapour
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A small river flowing into mist.
explanation.definitionFit: A brook is a small watercourse, as is a stream.

clue.text: Shambles getting yours truly on ship

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: yours truly is a jokey way of saying me
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Chaos ensues when the speaker boards a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess is a state of disorder, just as a shambles is.

clue.text: Early moves to screen commercial earlier

indicators.note: to screen means to hide behind, so the rearranged letters enclose the advert
moves says the letters of early are shifted into a new order

parts.note: an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: A TV channel brings an advert forward in the schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Early' looks like the definition, but it is the letters moved; the definition is 'earlier' at the end, and 'to screen' means to hide.
explanation.definitionFit: Already means by an earlier time, before now.

clue.text: Coffee: second of two cut

indicators.note: cut says the word loses its tail end

parts.note: the latter is the second of two things mentioned

explanation.surface: Ordering a coffee, someone picks the second of two and has it shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: A latte is an espresso drink made with steamed milk.

clue.text: Bingo audience

definitions.meaning: an old name for the game bingo, and the winner's call
a ... is the audience in a theatre, as in 'a full ...'

explanation.surface: The crowd at a bingo hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: the game of housey-housey and a theatre's spectators.

clue.text: Male is upset with son lacking in purpose

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A father is upset that his son is drifting without direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reads as the father's mood but signals the rearranging; 'lacking in purpose' is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Aimless describes someone without any goal or direction.

clue.text: Spattered red wine covering complete quilt

indicators.note: covering says the rearranged letters go round the other piece
spattered means splashed about, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: to do a task is to complete it

explanation.surface: Red wine is splashed all over the bedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complete' looks like an adjective for the quilt but is the verb do, as in doing a job.
explanation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a thick bed quilt, originally filled with feathers from the eider duck.

clue.text: Boy on a register, supporter of the Stuarts

parts.note: Roy is a boy's name
a list is a register of names

explanation.surface: A boy's name is entered on a register of Stuart supporters.
explanation.definitionFit: Royalists backed the Stuart kings against Parliament in the English Civil War.

clue.text: Ruin mood and rioting starts

indicators.note: starts says to take the opening letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A bad mood and street riots wreck everything.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar something is to spoil or damage it.

clue.text: Paste: fix a large plateful, last of spaghetti

parts.note: to rig something is to fix it dishonestly
a ton is a great amount, as in 'tons of food'

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word spaghetti

explanation.surface: Someone fixes a big plate of pasta, finishing with spaghetti.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paste' is the Italian plural of pasta, which literally means paste or dough.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigatoni are ridged tubes of pasta, and pasta is Italian for a dough or paste.

clue.text: Take in sci-fi film about aliens primarily

indicators.note: about means around, so the film's letters go round that letter

parts.note: ET is Spielberg's science-fiction film about an alien

indicators.note: primarily says to use only the opening letter of aliens

explanation.surface: Absorbing a science-fiction film about extraterrestrials.
explanation.definitionFit: To take food in is to consume it.

clue.text: Time a poet composed something for the breakfast table?

indicators.note: composed means put together, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A poet writes verse over breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot for brewing tea is a familiar sight on a breakfast table; the question mark flags the loose description.

clue.text: Hiding expression of pain, crying — turning somewhat pale?

indicators.note: hiding says one piece is tucked away inside the other

parts.note: crying out is yelling
ow is what someone says when hurt

explanation.surface: Someone stifles a cry of pain while shouting, going pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellowing paper or skin takes on a faded yellow tinge, a drift towards pallor.

clue.text: Beastly offspring, rubbish

definitions.meaning: the young born to an animal at one time

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a nasty animal's young.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are everyday senses: puppies or kittens born together, and discarded waste.

clue.text: Flowers: one comes up

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
something that comes up rises

explanation.surface: A gardener notes that a single bloom has sprouted.
explanation.definitionFit: Irises are flowering plants with sword-shaped leaves.

clue.text: Type of onion: chance to consume the lot

indicators.note: to consume means to swallow up, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a shot is an attempt or chance, as in 'have a shot'
the lot means all of it

explanation.surface: A greedy diner gets a chance to eat every last bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallot is a small mild variety of onion.

clue.text: Silly originally, time to get wise

indicators.note: originally says to take the opening letter of silly

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone foolish at first grows wiser over the years.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage as an adjective means showing deep wisdom.

clue.text: Author moving quickly

explanation.surface: A writer who works at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: the satirist and the adjective for speedy.

clue.text: Somewhat talentless, a shocking band

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a pop group as untalented and dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks musical; it is a strip of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a long strip of fabric worn round the waist or over a shoulder.

clue.text: Twelve dozen glaring

explanation.surface: A large batch that is impossible to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: the counting unit of 144 and the adjective for blatant.

clue.text: Nearest orders coming from China, perhaps?

indicators.note: orders is a verb here, arranging the letters of nearest in a fresh sequence

explanation.surface: Takeaway orders from the closest Chinese restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: China lies in the East, so things from there are Eastern; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
